full_judgment:
Afzal Hossain Ahmed J: This Rule, at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner, was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 29-3-2004 passed by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh in Family Appeal No. 21 of 2002 allowing the appeal in part should not be set aside and/or such other order or further order/orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. The Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh on hearing both the parties and considering the facts, circumstances and evidence adduced by the parties, by his judgment and decree dated 20-2-2002, decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff as claimed by her. 

 5. Being aggrieved by that judgment and decree, the defendant preferred appeal and the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh in Family Appeal No. 21 of 2002 allowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 29-3-2004 reversing part of the decision of the Family Court against which the plaintiff filed the instant Revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mr Md Omar Ali Khan, the learned. Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner, submits that the appellate Court below misread, misinterpreted, misconstrued the evidence on record and without any evidence before him modified the judgment and decree passed by the Family Court below and that the appellate Court below failed to consider that the defendant-opposite party could not prove the divorce as claimed to have been pronounced by him by producing the Talaknama before the trial Court and thereby committed error of law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr Khan has lastly submitted that the photo copy of the so-called Talaknama and the registered postal receipts filed by the appellant- opposite party in the appellate Court intending to show that the so-called Talaknama has been sent to the petitioner and the Chairman of the local Union Parishad have been taken into consideration by the Appellate Court though the said documents were not proved and taken into evidence according to the provision of the Law of Evidence and thus, the appellate Court below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, impugned judgment and decree are not sustainable in law. 

 9. Three witnesses from each side were examined in this case. It appears from the judgment and decree passed by the Family Court below that this Court, considering the facts, circumstances and evidence on record, decreed the suit against the defendant for payment of dower money of Taka 1,00,005 and maintenance cost of Taka 2,000 per month till the marriage subsists with arrear allowance at the same rate for 31 months to the plaintiff-petitioner. It appears from the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below that this Court allowed the appeal-in-part modifying the decree allowing maintenance at the rate of Taka 2,000 per month till May, 1999 and also allowed dower money of Taka 1,00,005 to the plaintiff. It appears that the defendant-appellant has not filed a single scrap of paper in the Family Court below to show that he had pronounced the divorce repudiating his marriage with the plaintiff. In the appellate Court the defendant-appellant, however, filed a photo copy of the Talaknama and registered postal receipts with a view to show that by executing that Talaknama he repudiated his marriage with the plaintiff having sent copies thereof to the plaintiff-petitioner and the Chairman of the local Union Parishad. It appears that the Appellate Court below having taken those documents filed by the appellant-opposite party into evidence considered those in favour of the appellant-opposite party though no application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for acceptance of those documents as additional evidence was filed and the same were filed only by a firisti as appears from the order No. 26 dated 10-3-2004 of the appellate Court below, even those documents were not proved into evidence by examining any witness. 

 10. In order to pronounce effective judgment, additional evidence may be adduced at the appellate stage under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Section 67 of the Evidence Act, 1872 provides as to the manner of proof of certain document. Unless a document is proved in accordance with law such document cannot be admitted into evidence forming the basis of a decree. Mere filing of document is not sufficient to satisfy the requirement of law. 

 11. Mr Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, in appreciation of his submission, as above, has cited a decision in the case of Atul Gomez vs Julian Rozario reported in 6 MLR (AD) 46 wherein their Lordships have held that the High Court Division, in the circumstances, rightly interfered with the judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court on mere filing of the documents without proper proof thereof. 

 13. It appears from the impugned judgment passed by the Appellate Court below that the appellant-respondent simply filed a photo copy of the so called Talaknama and some registered postal receipts without making any obligation for acceptance of the same into evidence at the Appellate stage as required under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure and without proving the same by examining any witness competent to prove the documents. Unless a document is proved in accordance with law such document cannot be admitted into evidence forming the basis of a decree which precisely has happened in the instant case. It is found that the appellate Court below without taking the photo copy of the so-called Talaknama and the postal receipts into evidence in accordance with law, forming basis thereupon interfered with the judgment and decree passed by the Family Court below holding that the appellant-opposite party had pronounced divorce repudiating his marriage with the plaintiff-petitioner with effect from 16-2-2000 and thereby the appellate Court below has committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below is not sustainable in law. 

 14. In this regard, we keep on record that both the Family Court as well as the appellate Court below concurrently found that the plaintiff is entitled to get dower money to the tune of Taka 1,00,005 from the defendant. In addition to that, we direct the defendant to pay maintenance to the plaintiff at the rate of Taka 2,000 per month so long the marriage subsists including the arrear maintenance as decreed by the Family Court below.
